competitive_alternatives.name: Manual content operations + external tooling
competitive_alternatives.what_customers_do: Enterprise marketing teams assemble pages manually in AEM (4 hours per page), then export to external point-solution tools (Jasper for content, Adobe Target for testing, Siteimprove for accessibility, Slack for approvals, Salesforce for campaign execution). Each tool operates independently; teams manually coordinate across systems.
limitations: Manual content assembly takes 4+ hours per page
External point-solutions require separate vendor management
No unified orchestration — teams manually coordinate
Accessibility/compliance are post-publication, not built-in
No scaling without proportional headcount growth

competitive_alternatives.name: Single-vendor bundled platforms (Adobe CX Enterprise, Sitecore AEM, Optimizely One)
competitive_alternatives.what_customers_do: Customers consolidate to a single platform vendor hoping to eliminate tool fragmentation. But monolithic platforms require expensive license upgrades, lock teams into vendor roadmaps, and deliver 'jack-of-all-trades' features that don't specialize in content operations orchestration.
limitations: Expensive platform upgrades and bundling tactics
Vendor lock-in — difficult to switch
Generic features that don't specialize in operations
Still require manual handoffs across layers
GenStudio (Adobe's agentic layer) is 12-24 months away

competitive_alternatives.name: Hiring more marketing operations staff
competitive_alternatives.what_customers_do: As content production scales, enterprises add QA specialists, compliance auditors, and content coordinators to manage manual workflows. This adds headcount cost, slows hiring velocity, and doesn't fundamentally solve the production bottleneck.
limitations: Cost: $250K-$500K+ per additional QA/compliance specialist
Slow hiring cycles for specialized roles
Doesn't address the fundamental process bottleneck
Manual QA is inconsistent and error-prone
Scaling content requires proportional headcount scaling

competitive_alternatives.name: Point-solution compliance tools (Siteimprove, Deque, Applitools)
competitive_alternatives.what_customers_do: Enterprises use post-publication compliance scanners and accessibility auditors that run after pages go live. These tools detect violations but require manual remediation and legal review.
limitations: Reactive (post-publication) compliance checking
Violations found after pages are live
Manual remediation workflow required
Increases compliance risk and litigation exposure
No integration with content authoring or deployment

competitive_alternatives.name: Agency partnerships (like WPP Open)
competitive_alternatives.what_customers_do: Enterprises outsource content production to agencies (like WPP) that codify agentic workflows internally. This works for large-scale productions but creates vendor dependency, loses operational control, and adds significant service fees.
limitations: High service fees and vendor dependency
Loss of operational control
Best for episodic campaigns, not continuous operations
Slow iteration cycles
IP/know-how stays with agency

competitive_alternatives.name: Status quo: Keep manual processes as-is
competitive_alternatives.what_customers_do: Enterprises continue with manual content assembly, QA, accessibility audits, and deployment. As content scale grows, manual overhead grows proportionally.
limitations: Unscalable — manual effort grows with volume
Compliance risk increases with scale
Team burnout from repetitive manual work
Slow time-to-market for campaigns
Competitors adopting automation gain advantage
